title: AI Archiving Assistant
summary: An independent concept/prototype exploring how an archivist could review AI-suggested tags, inspect supporting context, and approve or revise metadata before applying it.

hero.title: AI Archiving Assistant
hero.subtitle: Exploring how people could review AI suggestions without giving up control of the archive.
hero.summary: This independent design concept explores archive tagging, review queues, and human approval. It is not a client deployment. The workflow below describes the proposed experience, with validation still to do.

overview.title: Review suggestions before they become metadata
overview.description: The intended user is an archivist reviewing incoming material. The concept asks how AI could suggest tags while keeping the source material, uncertainty, and final approval visible.

challenge.title: A suggestion needs enough context to be checked
challenge.description: The design assumes that inconsistent metadata and uncertain suggestions could make review difficult. These are starting assumptions for a concept, not findings from a client research study.
list: A reviewer needs to see the asset and its suggested metadata together.
An uncertain suggestion should remain open to correction or manual review.
Approving a suggestion should be an explicit action.

solution.title: Inspect, revise, approve
solution.description: The concept keeps the review task in one flow. AI suggestions remain provisional until a person decides what to keep.

steps.title: Choose an item to review
steps.description: A review queue would separate straightforward items from suggestions needing closer attention.

steps.title: Inspect the asset and suggested tags
steps.description: The reviewer would examine supporting context, accept useful suggestions, and edit or remove unsuitable tags.

steps.title: Approve or keep in review
steps.description: An explicit approval would apply the chosen metadata. Unresolved items would remain available for manual review.

interaction.title: Design decisions in the concept
interaction.description: These patterns are intended to make the review process understandable. Their usefulness needs testing.

cards.title: Context beside the suggestion
cards.description: Keep the original asset visible so reviewers can assess the suggestion without relying only on a confidence score.

cards.title: A visible correction path
cards.description: Give editing and rejection the same clear place in the flow as approval.

cards.title: Human approval
cards.description: Make the reviewer’s final decision explicit before proposed metadata is applied.

impact.title: What I would test next
impact.description: There are no measured accuracy, adoption, or time-saving results for this concept.
results: Observe whether an archivist can review an item, correct an unsuitable tag, and complete the task without help.
Check whether reviewers can distinguish a suggestion from approved metadata.
Test uncertain and incorrect suggestions, including when reviewers choose manual review.

conclusion.title: Current status
conclusion.description: Independent concept/prototype. The next step is testing the proposed review flow with intended users before making claims about usefulness or performance.
